slides.title: ATAK, built for everyone
slides.html: ATAK is the map app TAK users share positions and marks on. It is built for every possible user, so one enemy mark takes many taps.

slides.title: An easier ATAK
slides.html: OpenDefence Main is a plugin for ATAK that does the common things in a few taps. Mark the enemy, send the mark and read what others report.

slides.title: The thumb bar
slides.html: OpenDefence Main's buttons sit on the thumb bar at the bottom left of the map. Inbox is on top and Markers below.

slides.title: Plugins join in
slides.html: Other OpenDefence plugins add their buttons beside Markers, such as Drones from OpenDefence UAVOps and Voice from OpenDefence Voice. Here Drones has opened OpenDefence UAVOps.

slides.title: One way of working, shared
slides.html: Learn Markers, Send to…, where you share a mark, and the Inbox once. Plugins such as Drones work through them, so a drone request's answer shows in the same Inbox.

slides.title: Built for military use
slides.html: Markers draws NATO's standard military symbols (APP-6D). Here the Size sheet offers an enemy Mech. infantry in each size.

slides.title: Read by every TAK user
slides.html: Every mark goes out in TAK's standard format. Users of plain ATAK, of WinTAK on Windows and of iTAK on iPhone, allies included, see the right symbol without OpenDefence Main.

slides.title: Set for the operation
slides.html: Your admins pick the symbols that come first for the whole operation, like these enemy favourites.
